verdict: Lead volume has collapsed this week; Google spend is being corrected now.
narrative: This period delivered 21 leads at a cost per lead of $168.80 — well above the $28–$42 range seen in early July, and the last four days produced zero leads despite nearly $612 in spend. The primary driver is Google Ads: one Local Services campaign absorbed $2,304 of your $2,900 Google budget over 28 days with almost no conversion return, and Google went completely dark on July 29. That campaign is under immediate review and budget is being redirected toward what is actually producing results. Separately, a gap in lead intake ownership is being confirmed to ensure any leads that do arrive are followed up promptly. Next week should reflect corrected Google spend allocation and a clearer picture of Meta's output as that channel is the sole source of tracked leads right now.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all from Meta
cost per lead this period, up sharply from the $28–$42 baseline in early July
spent on one Google Local Services campaign with near-zero leads returned

watch_item.issue: Zero leads over the last four days while spend continued — Google's top campaign misfired and lead intake ownership is unconfirmed.
watch_item.fix: The Google Local Services campaign is being reviewed and reallocated this week, and intake coverage is being clarified to ensure arriving leads are not lost in the pipeline.
